claude_proposed_widenings.name: hp_pool
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Lay On Hands uses a replenishable numeric HP point pool (capacity = 5 × paladin level) that is drawn down by variable amounts across multiple uses per rest cycle. UseCountResource models discrete use-counts decremented by 1 per activation; it cannot represent a pool where each activation depletes an arbitrary number of HP (1 to pool_remaining). The pool is shared across both uses (heal HP and cure condition), so the resource atom must support partial draws, not just fixed-use-count decrement.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level

claude_proposed_widenings.name: remove_condition (ClassFeatureEffect variant)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The secondary use expends 5 HP from the pool to remove the Poisoned condition without restoring HP. ClassFeatureEffect only has heal_hp and grant_extra_action; neither represents condition removal. A remove_condition variant requires at minimum a condition name (Condition) and a pool cost (number of HP spent), and must be expressible as an alternative to heal_hp that draws from the same hp_pool.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You can also expend 5 Hit Points from the pool of healing power to remove the Poisoned condition from the creature; those points don't also restore Hit Points to the creature.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: variable_draw (DiceAmount variant)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The heal amount is 'up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool' — a player-chosen integer between 1 and pool_remaining at activation time. DiceAmount offers fixed, threshold_tiers, and linear_per_level — all compute a determined amount. None express a bounded player choice. This variant would need a reference to the hp_pool atom and a draw semantic (e.g., draw: 'up_to_pool_remaining').
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool of healing to restore a number of Hit Points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool

claude_proposed_widenings.name: dual_use_pool_draw
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Lay On Hands presents two mutually-exclusive activation modes (heal HP vs. cure Poisoned condition) both drawing from a single shared hp_pool. ClassFeatureActivationMechanics has a single effect field with no branching or choice mechanism. A dual-use subgraph needs: (1) a choice node (player selects heal or cure), (2) each branch specifying a pool draw cost and effect, (3) the shared hp_pool resource consumed by whichever branch fires.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you can touch a creature … and draw power from the pool … [to heal] … You can also expend 5 Hit Points from the pool … to remove the Poisoned condition
